title: Context rollforward safety‑net for long‑context KV onboarding and version pin commits
creator: Priya Sharma
description: Problem: onboarding new KV cache profiles and pinning model versions for long context models has occasional regressions in tail latency when sequences exhibit heavy cross‑span dependencies. We need a 'rollforward' safety net that allows committing a pinned profile and model version while automatically creating short‑lived fallback artifacts and a pressure test run before traffic ramp. This ticket defines design, implementation tasks, and acceptance criteria for the rollforward/safety‑net flow and the publishing signals that inform Console and the profile registry.
acceptance_criteria: A rollforward workflow exists that can atomically pin a model+kv profile and simultaneously register a fallback profile that will be used automatically under SLO breaches
A pressure‑test harness runs a sampled replay of long‑context sequences for the candidate pin and produces a stability score (latency P95/P99, kv hit rate, memory churn)
On successful rollforward publish, Console shows the candidate pin state: staged -> active -> stable with timestamps and links to pressure‑test artifacts
If pressure test fails or early production SLO breaches occur, the system auto‑rolls to the fallback profile and creates an incident stub with diagnostics
All metadata written to profile registry includes sequence distribution fingerprint, anchor heuristics used, and commit SHA for model variant
Runbook for oncall explaining how to manually force rollback/rollforward is authored and linked from Console
tasks: Design API extension for Profile Registry: publishWithFallback(profile, fallbackProfile, testSuiteRef)
Implement pressure‑test harness that replays sampled long sequences (support for multi‑span anchors and cross‑span KV accesses)
Add stability score computation and thresholds (P95 latency, P99 latency, kv hit ratio drop)
Console UI: Add staged pin timeline and direct link to pressure test results and artifacts
Runtime: implement fast switch to fallback profile with metric tags (rollback_reason, triggered_by)
E2E test: simulate a failing profile and verify auto‑roll to fallback and incident creation
Docs: PRD update + runbook + migration notes for existing pinned profiles
implementation_notes: Pressure test will run in a sandbox cluster using the same serving runtime binary to avoid binary drift
We will sample sequences using existing sequence distribution service; ensure sampling preserves anchor boundaries and span markers
Fallback profiles should be conservative: smaller context pin window and higher eviction aggressiveness to reduce memory churn
Stability score should be a weighted metric: 50% latency tail, 30% kv hit rate delta, 20% memory churn
Committed metadata will include: model_variant_sha, profile_version, fingerprint_hash, sampled_sequence_histogram_url
Proposal: label the commit in registry with a 'rollforward_id' UUID for tracing across subsystems
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Decision: prefer rollforward (publish + fallback) over blocking publish. Rationale: reduces human blockers and enables safe fast iteration for power users
Tradeoff: additional storage cost for pressure test artifacts vs. reduced incident MTTR. Chosen threshold: keep last 30 artifacts per model
Decision: use existing sequence sampler service rather than shipping a new sampling job to reduce surface area
Tradeoff: automated roll to fallback may hide regressions for low‑traffic customers. Mitigation: surface incidents prominently and notify workspace owners
risks: Incorrect sampling leading to false confidence: ensure sample diversity across customers and payload shapes
Rollback thrashing if thresholds are too tight: implement cooldown window and max one auto‑rollback per hour per model
Security: pressure‑test artifacts may contain sensitive tokens — ensure scrubber and KMS policy applied
Operational: increased write load on profile registry during mass rollforwards — monitor and rate limit
notes: Benchmarks: early local runs show P95 increase of 12% under naive pin for a sampled 32k token longseq workload; fallback profile reduces P95 to baseline
We should coordinate with Dedicated team for customers with reserved pools to avoid surprising capacity impacts
Consider exposing an opt‑out flag for auto‑fallback for enterprise customers who prefer manual control
